findings.title: App-role membership in pg_read_all_data / pg_write_all_data is not reported
findings.detail: APP_ROLE_PRIVILEGED flags membership only in ownerRole or in a superuser or BYPASSRLS role. If a later change grants ursitoare_app the predefined pg_read_all_data or pg_write_all_data role, the app role can read or write tenant_route directly. The catalog check stays clean in that case, because has_table_privilege on tenant_route may report the predefined-role grant inconsistently, and no role rule covers it. (waived by the delegate (claude-fable-5-1 via claude-code): The finding is waived. The requirement "The runtime role is unprivileged" names a closed list of role conditions: missing, superuser, BYPASSRLS, owning a relation, or membership in ursitoare_owner or in a superuser or BYPASSRLS role. The checker implements exactly that list, and membership in pg_read_all_data or pg_write_all_data is not in it, which is why no scenario pins it down. The project assigns stray memberships of the app role to a different layer: the database specification requires ensureRoles to revoke every membership of the app role, and its repair scenario uses GRANT pg_read_all_data TO ursitoare_app as the very case that must be undone; roles.ts revokes each pg_auth_members row of the app role. The migration precondition and the health check use the same three membership conditions as the catalog checker, so the rule set is a deliberate project decision, not an omission of this unit. The judge's claim that has_table_privilege reports the predefined-role grant inconsisten)
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN the app role is a member of pg_read_all_data or pg_write_all_data THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports no app_role_privileged violation for that membership.

findings.title: A unique index that includes tenant_id but does not lead with it is reported
findings.detail: The spec says a unique index violates when it 'does not lead with or include tenant_id', which can be read either way. The code checks only indkey[0], so an index on (email, tenant_id) is reported.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a unique index holds tenant_id at a position other than the first THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports unique_not_tenant_leading for that index.

findings.title: A foreign key with tenant_id at a later position is accepted
findings.detail: The FK rule only requires tenant_id somewhere in conkey, mapped to the referenced tenant_id. No scenario pins down whether it must lead.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a foreign key holds tenant_id at a later position, mapped to the referenced table's tenant_id THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports no fk_not_tenant_scoped for it.

findings.title: security_invoker spellings other than true/on are not exempt
findings.detail: A view created WITH (security_invoker = 1) or 'yes' is stored with that literal, so a view that is in fact safe is reported as view_open_to_app.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a view granted to the app role has reloptions security_invoker=1 or security_invoker=yes THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports view_open_to_app for it.

findings.title: The materialized view probe reads bad_view, not ursitoare.tenant
findings.detail: The scenario says bad_mv is created 'over it', meaning ursitoare.tenant. The test builds it over bad_view instead. The catalog outcome is the same.

findings.title: fn that ends the transaction itself is not detected
findings.detail: inTransaction treats only a COMMIT tag of ROLLBACK as aborted. If fn runs its own ROLLBACK or COMMIT, the outer COMMIT gets a warning and the tag COMMIT, so the helper resolves, and any statements fn ran afterwards ran autocommitted without the transaction-local tenant. No scenario pins this down.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN fn runs its own ROLLBACK through tx and then returns a value THEN withTenantTx resolves with that value, then resets app.tenant_id to '' and releases the connection.

human.question: Q-002
human.reason: The finding is waived. The requirement "The runtime role is unprivileged" names a closed list of role conditions: missing, superuser, BYPASSRLS, owning a relation, or membership in ursitoare_owner or in a superuser or BYPASSRLS role. The checker implements exactly that list, and membership in pg_read_all_data or pg_write_all_data is not in it, which is why no scenario pins it down. The project assigns stray memberships of the app role to a different layer: the database specification requires ensureRoles to revoke every membership of the app role, and its repair scenario uses GRANT pg_read_all_data TO ursitoare_app as the very case that must be undone; roles.ts revokes each pg_auth_members row of the app role. The migration precondition and the health check use the same three membership conditions as the catalog checker, so the rule set is a deliberate project decision, not an omission of this unit. The judge's claim that has_table_privilege reports the predefined-role grant inconsisten

findings.title: App-role membership in pg_read_all_data / pg_write_all_data is not reported
findings.detail: APP_ROLE_PRIVILEGED flags membership only in ownerRole or in a superuser or BYPASSRLS role. If a later change grants ursitoare_app the predefined pg_read_all_data or pg_write_all_data role, the app role can read or write tenant_route directly. The catalog check stays clean in that case, because has_table_privilege on tenant_route may report the predefined-role grant inconsistently, and no role rule covers it.
evidence: src/tenancy/catalog.ts: AND (o.rolname = $2 OR o.rolsuper OR o.rolbypassrls)
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN the app role is a member of pg_read_all_data or pg_write_all_data THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports no app_role_privileged violation for that membership.

findings.title: A unique index that includes tenant_id but does not lead with it is reported
findings.detail: The spec says a unique index violates when it 'does not lead with or include tenant_id', which can be read either way. The code checks only indkey[0], so an index on (email, tenant_id) is reported.
evidence: src/tenancy/catalog.ts: WHERE (c.tenant_attnum IS NOT NULL AND i.indkey[0] = c.tenant_attnum) IS NOT TRUE
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a unique index holds tenant_id at a position other than the first THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports unique_not_tenant_leading for that index.

findings.title: A foreign key with tenant_id at a later position is accepted
findings.detail: The FK rule only requires tenant_id somewhere in conkey, mapped to the referenced tenant_id. No scenario pins down whether it must lead.
evidence: src/tenancy/catalog.ts: OR array_position(con.conkey, c.tenant_attnum) IS NULL
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a foreign key holds tenant_id at a later position, mapped to the referenced table's tenant_id THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports no fk_not_tenant_scoped for it.

findings.title: security_invoker spellings other than true/on are not exempt
findings.detail: A view created WITH (security_invoker = 1) or 'yes' is stored with that literal, so a view that is in fact safe is reported as view_open_to_app.
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN a view granted to the app role has reloptions security_invoker=1 or security_invoker=yes THEN checkTenancyCatalog reports view_open_to_app for it.

findings.title: The materialized view probe reads bad_view, not ursitoare.tenant
findings.detail: The scenario says bad_mv is created 'over it', meaning ursitoare.tenant. The test builds it over bad_view instead. The catalog outcome is the same.
evidence: src/tenancy/catalog.roles.test.ts: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW ursitoare.bad_mv AS SELECT * FROM ursitoare.bad_view

findings.title: fn that ends the transaction itself is not detected
findings.detail: inTransaction treats only a COMMIT tag of ROLLBACK as aborted. If fn runs its own ROLLBACK or COMMIT, the outer COMMIT gets a warning and the tag COMMIT, so the helper resolves, and any statements fn ran afterwards ran autocommitted without the transaction-local tenant. No scenario pins this down.
evidence:
src/tenancy/tx.ts: const committed = await client.query("COMMIT");
    if (committed.command === "ROLLBACK") {
findings.suggested_fix: WHEN fn runs its own ROLLBACK through tx and then returns a value THEN withTenantTx resolves with that value, then resets app.tenant_id to '' and releases the connection.

riskiest_assumptions: That src/tenancy/tx.ts (part 2) implements withTenantTx and inTransaction as the passing tests suggest; resolveTenantBy, ensureDefaultTenant and the route tests all depend on it.
That the gate's passing tx.test.ts tests ran against the committed tx.ts and a real Postgres, so the COMMIT command tag really is 'ROLLBACK' for an aborted transaction under node-postgres.
That src/tenancy/index.ts, not in the diff, already re-exports every function and type the tests import from the scaffold.
